rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alif-Lam-Ra are mysterious divine signs in the alphabetic letters that emerge from within and roll in people’s mouths.
rows.anchor: Allahu a‘lem bakınız içeriden gelip ağızlarda çalkanan o hecâ harfleri ne sırr-ı ilâhîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tilka refers to these surah verses as verses of the manifest Book.
rows.anchor: Bunlar bu الٓر yani bu sûre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mubin as an intransitive participle means self-evident, manifest in itself, and needing no explanation beyond itself.
rows.anchor: Lâzımdan “mübîn” nefsinde zâhir ve beyyin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a transitive participle, mubin means one that explains, displays, or distinguishes.
rows.anchor: Müte‘addîsi de beyan edici, izhar edici, ayırt edici demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mubin can also mean eloquent: able to express intended meaning beautifully and appropriately, with fluency and rhetoric.
rows.anchor: lisânı gayet güzel, murâdını yerine göre dilediği gibi anlatır, fasih ve beliğ mânasına gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is manifest in every sense, as guidance, light, criterion, wise Book, and detailed Book.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân-ı azîmüşşân hüdâ, nûr, furkan bir kitâb-ı hakîm, bir kitâb-ı mufassal olduğu gibi her mânasıyla bir kitâb-ı mübîndir de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its inimitability proves by its own existence, without another proof, that it is a Book sent down from God.
rows.anchor: kendinden başka hiçbir delîle muhtaç olmayacak surette bizzat kendi mevcûdiyetiyle isbâta kâfi bir kitaptır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like the light-image in 24:35, the Qur’an is self-evident, experimentally established, and a miracle beyond doubt.
rows.anchor: bu bizâtihi beyyin, bi’t-tecribe sâbit, lâ-raybe-fîh bir mucizedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It explains religious foundations and knowledge, including laws, hidden realms, unseen reports, and past narratives.
rows.anchor: ahkâm ve şerâyi‘, hafâyâ-yı mülk ü melekût, ahbâr-ı gaybiye, kısas-ı mâziye gibi usûl ve me‘ârif-i dîniyeyi beyan eden bir kitaptır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It distinguishes truth from falsehood, good from evil, right from wrong, and beauty from ugliness.
rows.anchor: hakkı bâtıldan, hayrı şerden, doğruyu eğriden, güzeli çirkinden ayırt eden bir kitaptır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic is an especially powerful vehicle of expression because of the quality and completeness of its alphabet, and the balance, breadth, originality, harmony, and variety of its words and derivations.
rows.anchor: hurûf-ı hecâsındaki ciyâdet ve tamâmiyet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic’s subtle distinctions in allusion and gender help clarity within concision; its particles, syntax, inflection, and varied constructions support precise expression.
rows.anchor: kinâyâtında tezkîr ü te’nîs vesâire gibi îcaz içinde vuzûha hizmet eden furûk-ı dakīka

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an was revealed in the clearest, finest, and most distinguished dialects of Arabic.
rows.anchor: Kur’an bu lisânın en açık, en güzel, en mümtaz lehçeleri üzerine nâzil olmuştur

rows.speaker: Ebî Hayyân
rows.claim: Elmalılı reports Abu Hayyan’s note that Arabe is the name of Ishmael and Abraham’s homeland; Arabic may therefore refer initially to the language of that region.
rows.anchor: Tefsîr-i Ebî Hayyân’da ihtar olunduğu üzere “Arabe” ismi vardır ki İsmâil b. İbrâhim aleyhimesselâm’ın diyârı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet’s line describes the Prophet’s conquest of Mecca and uses Arabe with a silent rā for metrical necessity.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah’ın Mekke’yi fethini anlatmış ve zarûret-i vezn için عَرَبَه’nin râ’sını sâkin kılmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s composition gave Arabic exceptional purity and sweetness and created a peerless rhetorical style that itself made Arab rhetoricians recognize its inimitability.
rows.anchor: nazm-ı Kur’an, lisân-ı Arabîye öyle yüksek bir nekāhat ve halâvet vermiş, öyle bedî‘bir üslûb-i beyan ibdâ‘eylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This eloquent-language sense of mubin is a special Qur’anic attribute, though the self-evident-proof sense also entails it.
rows.anchor: birinci mâna tesbit olunmak için Muâz b. Cebel radıyallâhu anh’tan mervî olduğu üzere bilhassa bu dördüncü mânaya işaret olunmuştur

rows.speaker: Muâz b. Cebel
rows.claim: A report from Muadh is invoked to highlight the Qur’an’s eloquence as a particular sense of mubin.
rows.anchor: Muâz b. Cebel radıyallâhu anh’tan mervî olduğu üzere bilhassa bu dördüncü mânaya işaret olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yunus and Hud are more associated with the Qur’an’s wisdom, while Yusuf is especially associated with its eloquent expression.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Yûsuf da Kur’ân’ın daha ziyade hüsn-i beyan vasfıyla alâkadar olan âyetlerindendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God revealed the Qur’an in Arabic together with its Arabic wording, not merely its meanings.
rows.anchor: yani yalnız mânasını değil, Arabî olan nazmıyla birlikte makrû’ olarak indirdik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation calls people to understand, use reason, and recognize that the Qur’an is from God.
rows.anchor: iyi anlayasınız veya aklınızı isti‘mâl edesiniz de şimdi ihtar olunacağı üzere bunun Allah’tan olduğunu bilesiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Yusuf story is inherently full of lessons, and its finest narration is in this surah and this Qur’an; no other book tells it so beautifully.
rows.anchor: mantûkunca haddizâtında çok ibretli pek güzel bir kıssa olduğu gibi bunun en güzel beyânı da bu sûrede, bu Kur’an’dadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah itself is part of the manifest Book and was revealed to Muhammad as Qur’anic revelation in both wording and meaning.
rows.anchor: bu sûre de sana Kur’an vahyiyle, yani nazm u mânası birlikte makrû’ olarak vahyedilmiş bir Kur’an olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet had no prior awareness of this story—he had neither heard nor imagined it—so it was neither borrowed from another source nor invented as a novel.
rows.anchor: ne başka bir menba‘dan ahz u intihal olunmuş bir nakil, ne de senin tarafından tasavvur ve tasvir olunmuş bir roman

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its peerless expression, recited revelation, and report of the unseen are three clear proofs that it is a divine gift.
rows.anchor: böyle bir hüsn-i beyan, böyle bir vahy-i makrû’, böyle bir gayb haberi hiç şüphe yok ki bunların her biri ancak bir Allah vergisi olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s account is among the unseen reports revealed to Muhammad, as stated at the surah’s end.
rows.anchor: bu sûre ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ أَنۢبَآءِ ٱلْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ’dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is not fabricated speech, as the surah later states.
rows.anchor: tasavvur ve tasvir olunmuş bir roman değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahsan al-qasas can mean either the finest narration or the finest story, depending on its grammatical role.
rows.anchor: “Ahsenü’l-Kasas” en güzel anlatış veya en güzel kıssa mânasına mef‘ûl-i mutlak veya mef‘ûlün bih olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasas with fatḥa is originally a verbal noun meaning to follow something’s traces.
rows.anchor: Kāf’ın fethiyle “kasas” esasen masdardır. Ve asl-ı lügatta mânası bir şeyin izini tâkip ederek arkasına düşmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic phrase in 18:64 means that the two returned by following their tracks.
rows.anchor: “izlerini tâkip ederek geriye döndüler” demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command in 28:11 means to follow the trace and not lose sight of it.
rows.anchor: قُصِّيهِ izini tâkip et, arkasını bırakma demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From the sense of tracing comes qasas as a follow-worthy report or narrated account; qissa denotes the narrated story, and qisas is its plural.
rows.anchor: tâkibe şayan bir haber nakl ü hikâye etmek mânasına gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A qissa is fundamentally a state or affair worthy of being followed; the term also applies to stories written down or passed among people.
rows.anchor: da esasen izi tâkip olunmaya şâyan hâl ü şân mânasınadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Turkish usage, destan is familiar through wide circulation, efsane through unbelievable marvels, and kıssa through its lesson.
rows.anchor: “destan” tâbiri şöhret-i şâyi‘a itibariyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story qualifies as a qissa by possessing a quality worth following and recording; this gives the form special literary importance, while enduring beauty is rare.
rows.anchor: bir haber veya hikâyenin kıssa olabilmesi şâyân-ı tâkib ve tahrir bir haysiyeti hâiz olmasına mütevakkıftır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stories may be real or imagined, but the finest are true events eloquently depicted through the subtleties of their lasting beauty.
rows.anchor: Kıssaların hakīkīsi de hayâlîsi de vardır. Şüphe yok ki en güzel kıssalar hakīkī olanlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True beauty lies beyond imagination; imagination is beautiful only insofar as it symbolizes and exemplifies reality.
rows.anchor: hayâlin hüsnü ancak hakikate bir remz ü misâl olması itibariyledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf’s story portrays pure beauty’s journey to perfection and the soul that has seen eternal beauty looking with contempt on fleeting beauty.
rows.anchor: hüsn-i fânî cilvelerine nasıl bir nazar-ı ihtikar ile baktığını anlatan kıssa-i Yûsuf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Yusuf story is an eloquent account of an unseen truth that begins in an ambiguous divine symbol and gradually unfolds.
rows.anchor: gayb-ı haktan bir remz-i müteşâbih ile tecellîye başlayıp peyderpey inkişaf ederek meâlini bulmuş bir hakikatin beliğ bir beyânı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf’s dream symbolizes the future meaning and destiny of his pure beauty; the whole story similarly anticipates the complete meaning of Muhammad’s beauty.
rows.anchor: bütün tafsîlâtıyla kıssa-i Yûsuf da hüsn-i Muhammedînin meâl-i ekmeline öyle bir remz-i mütekaddim olarak nâzil olmuş bir hakīkat-i gaybiyedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This symbolic relation to Muhammad’s perfect beauty is especially why the Yusuf narrative is the finest of stories.
rows.anchor: bilhassa bu haysiyetledir ki ahsenü’l-kasastır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dream’s bowing heavenly bodies symbolize a future divine selection in which great people will be made subject to Yusuf.
rows.anchor: rüyada gördüğün gibi o yüksek ve parlak ecrâm-ı semâviyenin sana secde etmesi misâline benzer bedî‘bir ictibâ ile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dream is a representation of the future; Yusuf’s vision signals that God will grant him prophethood and make great people obey him.
rows.anchor: Yani rüya, istikbâlin bir misâlini görmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwil al-ahadith is the knowledge of determining the real-world meaning of words whose relation to events is hidden.
rows.anchor: nefiste hâdis olan ve vâkı‘a cihet-i ta‘alluku hafî bulunan sözlerin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This gifted knowledge may mean dream interpretation, understanding mysteries in revelation and divine signs, or discerning the eventual truth of unfolding events.
rows.anchor: rüya tâbir eylemek veya vahiy ve işârât-ı ilâhiyenin gavâmızını, ledünniyâtını anlamak veyahut hâdisâttan ileride varacağı hakikati anlamak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf will receive a distinguished share of this knowledge by divine gift rather than acquisition, confirming the truth of Yaqub’s prediction.
rows.anchor: ilm-i kesbî ile değil ilm-i vehbî ile böyle tâbirler, tefsirler yapıp şan alacaksın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing the blessing for Yusuf and Jacob’s family parallels the honor fully bestowed on Abraham and Isaac, including prophethood and honor in both worlds.
rows.anchor: nübüvvete muvaffak kılmış, dünya ve âhiret tam bir şeref ü şâna mazhar eylemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dream’s concise interpretation is given here; its detailed interpretation will occur through later events.
rows.anchor: İşte o rüyanın icmâlen tâbir ve tevili budur. Tafsîlen tevili ise ileride bilfiil vukū‘ât ile olacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what has happened and what will happen, acts with knowledge and wisdom, and knows who merits selection; the dream itself has wisdom.
rows.anchor: Her şeyi bilir: Olmuşu da bilir olacağı da bilir ve yaptığını ilim ve hikmetle yapar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later discussion of dream interpretation in the king’s court is relevant to this promise.
rows.anchor: İleride gelecek olan إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّءْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eleven stars in the dream represent Yusuf’s eleven brothers.
rows.anchor: olunduğu üzere biraderleri on bir idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of Yusuf and his brothers contains many signs for anyone seeking lessons.
rows.anchor: ale’l-umûm ibret arayanlara birçok ibret delilleri bulunduğu gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story gives signs to questioners about why the Israelites moved to Egypt, especially Meccan polytheists and the Jewish scholars prompting them, and thereby points to Muhammad’s messengership.
rows.anchor: Benî İsrâil’in Mısır’a ne sebeple geçtiğini sual eden sâillere, Mekke müşriklerine ve onlara telkīnâtta bulunan Yehûd ulemâsına risâlet-i Muhammediyeyi anlatacak alâmetler vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Usba means a tightly bound, mutually attached, zealous group.
rows.anchor: “Usbe” sıkı, birbirine sargın, mutaassıb bir cemaat

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By brother, Yusuf’s brothers mean Binyamin, who shared both parents with Yusuf.
rows.anchor: muradları ana baba bir biraderidir. Bunun da ismi Bünyamin olduğu mâruftur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other ten were paternal half-brothers; their wording treats Yusuf and Binyamin as brothers distinct from themselves.
rows.anchor: diğer on birader bu ikisinin yalnız baba bir üvey biraderleri olduklarından ikisini de kendilerine kardeş saymayarak aralarında böyle söylemişlerdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The buyer in Egypt was the Aziz, reportedly named Qitfir or Itfir; he had no children, and his wife was reportedly a virgin named Raʿil or Zuleyha.
rows.anchor: bu müşteri Azîz idi ve rivayet olunduğuna göre ismi “Kıtfîr” veya “Itfîr” imiş, zürriyeti yokmuş, zevcesi bâkirmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report calls three people exceptionally perceptive: the Aziz in recognizing Yusuf, Shuayb’s daughter in recognizing Moses, and Abu Bakr in appointing Umar.
rows.anchor: Demişlerdir ki nâsın en firâsetlisi üç zâttır: Birisi, Yûsuf’u teferrüsünde Azîz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd is the age when bodily strength intensifies and reaches maturity.
rows.anchor: eşüddüne erdi beden ve kuvvetinin şiddetlendiği kemâl çağına erişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The judgment and knowledge given to Yusuf mean exceptional authority and mastery, along with knowledge and prophethood.
rows.anchor: mümtaz bir hüküm ve ilim verdik yani fevkalâde bir nüfûz ve hâkimiyet ve bir ilm ü nübüvvet verdik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewards the virtuous by saving them from evil designs, establishing them in the land, granting authority and knowledge; He is doing likewise for Muhammad.
rows.anchor: Sû’-i kasd edenlerden kurtarır, arzda temkin eder, emrine gālib olur, hüküm ve ilim veririz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman of the house tried to obtain Yusuf sexually.
rows.anchor: evinde bulunduğu hanım nefsinden kâm almaya kalktı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf calls on God and regards his master as his benefactor, recalling that he gave Yusuf a good home and treated him well.
rows.anchor: benim efendim -veliyy-i nimetim mesvâmı ihsan etti- bana güzel baktı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Betraying one’s benefactor and repaying kindness with wrongdoing and ingratitude is oppression; oppressors do not prosper.
rows.anchor: döşeğe hıyanet, iyiliğe karşı kötülük, ihsâna nankörlük zulümdür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman’s intention was complete: she had given her heart to Yusuf and was wholly resolved on union, not merely testing his chastity.
rows.anchor: Ona tamamen gönlünü vermiş, bütün himmetiyle visâline azmetmişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects interpreting Yusuf’s conditional resolve as agreement with her; it should not be attributed to deficient virility or a natural shortcoming.
rows.anchor: bu onun erkeklik his ve kuvvetinin eksikliği gibi tabiatında bir noksanından dolayı zannedilmemelidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All external and internal causes of natural desire were present; only reverence for God restrained Yusuf, and he would have resolved if the act were lawful.
rows.anchor: Ancak Allah saygısından başka hiçbir mâni‘yoktu. Eğer fiili helâl olsa idi o da azmetmiş gitmişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf’s purity was a perfection: even then he saw his Lord’s proof and perceived the ugliness of the forbidden with certainty.
rows.anchor: Rabbinin burhânını görüyordu, haramın çirkinliğini bütün hakikatiyle ayne’lyakīn müşahede ediyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed Yusuf the proof to turn away evil, especially betrayal of kindness, and sexual indecency because he was among God’s purified servants.
rows.anchor: zira o Bizim hakikaten muhlas kullarımızdandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the lām opened, mukhlas means chosen and purified for God’s obedience; with it kasra, mukhlis means sincerely devoting religion to God.
rows.anchor: İsm-i mef‘ûl sîgası üzere lâm’ın fethiyle “muhlas”, sırf Allah’a itaat için seçilmiş lekesiz demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the mukhlas and mukhlis readings occur here.
rows.anchor: burada her iki kıraat de vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf’s chastity and purity are evident from his resistance under this coercion and threat.
rows.anchor: Yûsuf’un ismet ve nezâhetini anlamalı ki böyle bir ikrah ve tehdid karşısında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the woman admits she did not betray Yusuf in his absence, she does not thereby clear herself of her earlier words and deeds.
rows.anchor: hakkı itiraf ederken kendimi hıyanetten büsbütün tebri’e ve tenzih de etmem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human self naturally commands evil and inclines to desire, using its faculties in that direction; left to itself, it leads a person into wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: haddizâtında nefs-i beşer fenalığı kuvvetle âmirdir, fenalık kumandanıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those whom God especially mercies, such as Yusuf, are pure and protected; alternatively, God’s command overcomes the self-command, or the self becomes tranquil under it.
rows.anchor: ancak Rabbimin nefs-i Yûsuf gibi bilhassa rahmetiyle yarlığadığı nefisler pak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s forgiveness covers natural inclinations and His mercy keeps them from becoming deeds; He also forgives those who confess sin and seek pardon.
rows.anchor: temâyülâtı mağfiretiyle örttüğü ve cereyanlarına mâni‘olarak fiile çıkmaktan rahmetiyle muhafaza ettiği gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aziz’s wife confessed, repented, acknowledged the truth, and disclosed her faith; Yusuf’s divinely known purity became publicly manifest.
rows.anchor: Azîz’in kadını böyle itiraf ve istiğfar ederek hakkı ikrar ve imanını izhar etti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine love overcomes selfish desire; even hostile, jealous adversaries are compelled to acknowledge Yusuf’s virtue, as passion and anger fade before truth.
rows.anchor: aşk-ı Hak, aşk-ı nefsânîye nasıl galebe etti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the beauty of truth appears, passions, anger, and ego fall away, leaving no enduring attachment except love of God.
rows.anchor: ihtiraslar nasıl sönüyor, gayzlar nasıl siliniyor, benlikler nasıl kalkıyor da aşk-ı Hak’tan başka pâyidar olabilecek hiçbir alâka kalmıyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king wanted Yusuf brought so he could make him exclusively his own.
rows.anchor: kendim için istihlâs edeyim yani hâlis olarak kendime has kılayım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify this king with the earlier Aziz because Aziz can mean king, but Elmalılı rejects that reading as contrary to the Qur’an’s wording and context.
rows.anchor: ifâde-i Kur’ân’ın zâhirine muhaliftir. Zira

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aziz was a high-ranking vizier or emir near the Egyptian ruler, whereas the Malik was the monarch; reports name them Qitfir and Rayyan.
rows.anchor: Melik de hükümdarı demek olduğu anlaşılıyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reports give the Aziz’s name as Qitfir and the king’s as Rayyan.
rows.anchor: bazı rivayetlerde Azîz’in ismi “Kıtfir”, Melik’in ismi de “Reyyan” olduğu nakledilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the ruler Malik rather than Pharaoh may signal that he was not a tyrant in character, since Pharaoh’s title was notorious for oppression.
rows.anchor: nokta-i nazarından bir firavun olmadığına işaret edilmiş demektir

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Mujahid reportedly held that this king was Muslim.
rows.anchor: Nitekim Mücâhid’den bu Melik’in müslim olduğu menkuldür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title Malik may also imply that the Egyptian ruler was outside the Pharaoh dynasty and Coptic people.
rows.anchor: bu Mısır hükümdarının firavun sülâlesinden ve Kıbt kavminden olmadığına da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some histories identify the ruler as an Amalekite, likely among the Hyksos who came from Arabia, defeated Pharaohs, and reportedly ruled Egypt for about four hundred years.
rows.anchor: Arabistan tarafından geçip firavunlara galebe ederek dört yüz sene kadar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that the king was named Rayyan also supports an Arabic origin.
rows.anchor: İsminin Reyyan olduğu hakkındaki rivayet de bunun Arabî olduğuna delâlet eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects the view that this was the Pharaoh who lived until Moses: the Qur’an calls Yusuf’s ruler Malik but explicitly calls Moses’ enemy Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’da buna Firavun denilmemiş, hasm-ı Mûsâ’nın ise Firavun olduğu tansis edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This Malik esteemed Yusuf’s excellence even before seeing him, recognized him as unique in his time, and sought to make him his own.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Yûsuf’u henüz görmeden bi’l-vücûh kemâlâtına meclub oldu, zamanının vahîdi olduğunu anladı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed report says Yusuf wrote on the prison door that it was a dwelling of trials, grave of the living, gloating of enemies, and test of friends before leaving.
rows.anchor: burası belâlar konağı, diriler kabri, a‘dâ şemâteti, asdıkā tecribesidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says Yusuf prayed for his household and washed; he then greeted in Arabic and said the Hebrew prayer was his ancestors’ language.
rows.anchor: çıkmış, hânedânına dua etmiş, yıkanmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king tested Yusuf in many languages; Yusuf answered each one, astonishing the king.
rows.anchor: Melik birçok lisan bilirmiş, hepsinden söylemiş, o da cevap vermiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king asked Yusuf to recount his dream; Yusuf described its cows and ears of grain just as the king had seen them.
rows.anchor: rüyamı senden bizzat dinleyeyim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says Yusuf advised sowing abundantly in prosperous years, building storehouses, saving crops, and selling them during famine to enrich the treasury.
rows.anchor: kıtlık seneler gelince bu galleleri satarız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf asks to administer the revenues and expenditures of Egypt’s storehouses.
rows.anchor: bütün bu Mısır ülkesinin hazinelerinin îrad ve masraf-ı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hafiz and alim mean he preserves rights and trusts, protects the treasuries from the undeserving, and knows how they should be managed.
rows.anchor: Hukūk ve emânâtı iyi hıfzederim, hazineleri müstahik olmayanlardan iyi korur ve vücûh-ı tasarrufu pek iyi bilirim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not prove the king was unbelieving; Mujahid reportedly said he was Muslim.
rows.anchor: Fakat âyette bu Melik’in küfrüne dair delil yoktur. Bilakis Mücâhid’den islâm olduğu mervîdir

rows.speaker: bazı müfessirler
rows.claim: Some commentators say the king followed Yusuf’s counsel and submitted to him, so Yusuf requested complete authority.
rows.anchor: müfessirînin dedikleri gibi Melik, Hazret-i Yûsuf’un re’yine tâbi‘ve ona münkād olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking or accepting office is forbidden for the unqualified; the qualified may accept, should generally not seek it, but must seek it if no other qualified person is available.
rows.anchor: Ehliyeti olmayanlara velâyet haramdır. Tefvîzi de haram, talebi de haram, kabûlü de haramdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf sought office as a means to discharge the divine duty of implementing justice and right rulings.
rows.anchor: min tarafillah me’mur olduğu ahkâm-ı hakk u adlin icrâsına bir vesile bulmak için bu talebiyle o vecîbenin îfâsına müsâra‘at etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God established Yusuf in Egypt through his trustworthiness and knowledge, giving him a high station and power.
rows.anchor: Arz-ı Mısır’da yüksek bir müknet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse leaves the king’s explicit response unstated and attributes Yusuf’s rise directly to God: God prepared the means and made the king an instrument.
rows.anchor: Yûsuf’u bu suretle makām-ı iktidâra getiren Melik değil, Allahu azîmüşşân idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed report says the king gave Yusuf a crown, signet, sword, and jeweled golden throne; Yusuf accepted the throne and seal but said the crown was not his or his ancestors’ attire.
rows.anchor: Melik, Hazret-i Yûsuf’a bir taç giydirmiş, devlet mührünü çıkarıp parmağına geçirmiş, kılıç kuşatmış ve onun için inci ve yakut ile murassa‘altından bir serîr vaz‘etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says Yusuf used the throne to secure the kingdom and the seal to administer its affairs, then began work and established justice.
rows.anchor: serîr, bununla mülkü sağlamlarım. Mühür, bununla umûrunu tedbir ederim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says the people loved Yusuf, the country obeyed him, and the Aziz Qitfir died; the king then married Yusuf to Qitfir’s wife Raʿil, also called Zuleyha, who was reportedly still a virgin.
rows.anchor: Azîz Kıtfir vefat etmiş imiş, zevcesi Râ‘îl, nâm-ı diğer Züleyha, Melik tarafından Hazret-i Yûsuf’a tezvic edilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same report says Yusuf and Raʿil had two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh.
rows.anchor: bundan iki oğlu olmuş: Efrayim b. Yûsuf, Menşa b. Yûsuf

rows.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem
rows.claim: The Prophet reportedly said God would have installed Yusuf immediately had he not asked for the storehouses; his request delayed his appointment by a year.
rows.anchor: Resûl-i Ekrem sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den menkuldür ki “Allah, rahmet eylesin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf was already designated for the post, but seeking it was not obligatory because preparations for famine were the first priority and a year’s delay would not forfeit that benefit.
rows.anchor: haddizâtında bu iş için Hazret-i Yûsuf ta‘ayyün etmişti fakat kendisine talep farz olmamıştı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking immediately after leaving prison might cloud Yusuf’s standing; God intended him to be sought and appointed with still greater authority.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ onu daha yüksek bir nüfuz ve müknetle iş başına geçirecekti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf was so secure, loved, and powerful that he could reside wherever he wished and administer all of Egypt’s cities, towns, villages, and fields.
rows.anchor: şehirleri, kasabaları, kurâsı ve mezâri‘i ile bütün Mısır arazisi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine mercy as pure grace may be bestowed freely, without any human earning, in this world, the hereafter, or both; Yusuf’s prophethood and success first came this way.
rows.anchor: kesb-i abdin hiç dahli olmayarak mücerred takdîrin cebrî bir cilvesi olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is also mercy tied to human effort and good action under divine law; God does not waste the reward of those who do good.
rows.anchor: abdin kesbine, hüsn-i ameline terettüb eden ve binâen‘aleyh bir şer‘u kanun ile cereyan eyleyen rahmet-i rahîmiye vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s principle is linked to the declaration that God’s mercy is near those who do good.
rows.anchor: إِنَّ رَحْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ قَرِيبٌۭ مِّنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ’dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf was a sincere doer of good, so God rewarded him by bringing him honorably from prison and making him established and trusted.
rows.anchor: Yûsuf aleyhisselâm da hâlis muhlis muhsinlerden olduğu için Allah ecrini zâyi‘etmemiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised reward for the virtuous should not be reduced to finite worldly power and treasure, which are mixed with pain and eventually perish.
rows.anchor: böyle lezzet-i elem ile karışık dünya devlet ve hazineleri gibi haddizâtında mütenâhî ve binâen‘aleyh fâni ve zâyi‘olan dünya ecrinden ibaret zannedilmemelidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hereafter’s reward is better because it is lasting, eternal, pure, and wholly good.
rows.anchor: Çünkü dâimî, ebedî, hâlis, hayr-ı mahzdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That superior reward belongs to those who believe in God, His Messenger, and the hereafter, and make avoidance of idolatry and sins their habit.
rows.anchor: Allah’ı ve Resûlünü tasdik ile âhirete inanıp ittikāyı şi‘âr edinen, şirk ve seyyiâttan korunmak âdeti olan muhsinler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers should focus on Yusuf’s endless hereafter reward, not his worldly position, and strive for complete faith, Godfearingness, and excellence.
rows.anchor: asıl âhirette ereceği nâmütenâhî ecr-i ihsânı nazar-ı i‘tibâra almalı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The famine years had arrived, bringing people from everywhere to seek provisions from Yusuf.
rows.anchor: mukaddemâ haber verdiği kıtlık seneleri hulûl etmiş olmakla zahîre için her taraftan gelip Yûsuf’a müracaat ediyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf immediately recognized his brothers; they had apparently given their identities when entering, and their appearance had not changed beyond recognition.
rows.anchor: bir değişiklik yokmuş ve zaten birini tanımış olsa hepsini tanıyacağı derkâr idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers did not recognize Yusuf because they had left him as a child and now met him in an unfamiliar condition and position.
rows.anchor: çünkü o çocukken ayrılmış, tanıyamayacakları bir hâl ve makamda bulunuyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise made when Yusuf was thrown into the well—to inform them of their deed while they remained unaware—was beginning to come true.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh sûrenin başında geçtiği üzere Yûsuf kuyuya atıldığı sırada kendisine vahyedilmiş olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As he finished preparing their provisions, Yusuf asked them to bring their other paternal brother, Binyamin, whom they had said was dear to their father.
rows.anchor: demiş oldukları kardeşi Bünyamin idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The visitors were the brothers who had taken Yusuf to the well; Binyamin was not among them.
rows.anchor: gelenler mukaddemâ Yûsuf’u götürüp kuyuya atanlar idi, içlerinde bu yoktu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had probably mentioned another brother while presenting their identities or needs, allowing Yusuf to ask for him without revealing himself.
rows.anchor: bir kardeşleri daha olduğunu söylemiş olmalılar ki Yûsuf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf’s familiarity could have seemed to the brothers like information gained through outside inquiry, leaving them astonished.
rows.anchor: haklarında hâricen yapılmış bir tahkik ve istihbâra

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His indefinite wording, a brother of yours from your father, acts as though he does not know Binyamin, marks his isolation, hints at Yusuf’s own kinship, and encourages them to bring the beloved brother.
rows.anchor: ma‘rife olarak بِأَخِيكُمْ “kardeşinizi” demeyip de kat‘-ı izâfetle nekre olarak بِأَخٍۢ لَّكُم demesi de çok mânidardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf says he gives full measure: he avoids injustice and misuse, gives neither less nor more, and wants to provide for later arrivals as well.
rows.anchor: Haksızlığa, sû’-i isti‘mâle meydan bırakmıyor, tam ölçüyor, vefâ ettiriyorum

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He had hosted and honored the brothers; he mentions his generosity not to boast, but to explain why he cannot give more and persuade them to bring Binyamin.
rows.anchor: hânesinde misafir etmiş, ziyafet vermiş, ikram ve ihsanda bulunmuş ve bunu bir minnet makamında değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they do not bring Binyamin, they will receive no grain from Yusuf; they will not even be able to obtain provisions elsewhere in Egypt or approach him for favor.
rows.anchor: Mısır toprağında bir kile zahîre almanız ihtimâli yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers promise to persuade their father for Binyamin, although he may not want to let him go, and say they will do it.
rows.anchor: varınca onun için babasına murâvede edeceğiz yani onu babası yanından bırakmak istemez amma kandırmak çaresine bakacağız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf’s attendants were the servants who measured the grain and managed the brothers’ provisions.
rows.anchor: zahîrelerini ölçen ve techîzâtlarıyla meşgul olan bendegânına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf secretly returned the brothers’ merchandise to their baggage as a further act of generosity.
rows.anchor: el altından böyle gizli bir ihsanda daha bulunmuştu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He hoped that finding their money restored would delight them and prompt them to return with Binyamin.
rows.anchor: ellerinde hazır bir sermaye bulacak ve dediği gibi biraderini alarak dönüp gelmeye şitâb edeceklerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although one might expect Yusuf to reveal himself and invite his father immediately, uncertainty remained about whether Yaqub would come, whether the family could move, and what political conditions allowed.
rows.anchor: Acaba gelecek miydi? Hânedânını Mısır’a nakletmek mümkin olacak mıydı? Ahvâl-i umûmiye, şerâit-i siyâsiye nelere müsâid idi?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In divine wisdom Binyamin had to come first; Yaqub’s added separation from Binyamin completed the causes of reunion and prepared the family to feel the final joy fully.
rows.anchor: hicrân-ı Yûsuf’a bir de hicrân-ı Bünyamin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf’s arrangements were not his own independent plan but proceeded by revelation, as the following verses make clear.
rows.anchor: kendiliğinden değil, biraz sonra gelecek âyetlerden anlaşılacağı üzere min tarafillah vahiy ile cereyan etmiştir
